description:
pkix-ct/src/verify.rs:837-857 — docstring (lines 839-844) says: "RFC 6962 §3.5 / §6.2 (and CT log lifecycle documentation) describe usable_from/retired_at as inclusive lower and upper bounds: SCTs timestamped at or after usable_from and strictly before retired_at are trustworthy."

The phrase "inclusive lower and upper bounds" is wrong/contradictory. The code (and the very next clause "at or after usable_from and strictly before retired_at") describes a half-open interval [usable_from_ms, retired_at_ms): inclusive lower, EXCLUSIVE upper.

The test verify.rs:1087-1099 ("log_window_upper_bound_exclusive") confirms exclusive upper. The text is mis-edited: someone wrote "inclusive lower and upper" when they meant "inclusive lower, exclusive upper".

Suggested fix: "usable_from_ms as an inclusive lower bound and retired_at_ms as an exclusive upper bound" matches the code and the tests. Two-word change.

Why this matters: a contributor reading the doc to add a new boundary test could easily pick the wrong semantics for retired_at. A user filing an issue about a borderline SCT would expect to be told "exclusive" — current text says "inclusive" and the issue reporter would believe their case was a bug.
title: log_window_contains semantic ambiguity: docstring says "inclusive lower and upper bounds" but code is [lo, hi)
